Success in 2026 requires preparation. Your maintenance activities must be documented and aligned with official standards to secure financial benefits and prove compliance.

A Baseline Thermal Scan records your cooling tower’s current approach, which is the temperature difference between the cold water outlet and the ambient wet-bulb temperature. This measurement establishes the system’s current thermal performance, providing a reliable reference point to track efficiency improvements over time. By understanding the baseline, operators can identify underperforming units, detect early signs of fouling or scaling in the cooling tower fill media, and plan targeted maintenance or upgrades. Regular thermal scans help optimize heat transfer, reduce energy consumption, and maximize operational efficiency for industrial facilities.

Digital Logbook Integration involves implementing an automated system to record all cooling tower maintenance activities, water quality measurements, and energy usage data. Unlike traditional paper logs, a digital logbook provides real-time visibility into system performance and maintenance history. It ensures compliance with environmental regulations, simplifies reporting for audits, and offers detailed insights into operational trends. By integrating sensors, IoT devices, or software dashboards, facilities can detect anomalies early, schedule timely interventions, and maintain optimal thermal performance. Digital logbooks also support predictive maintenance strategies, protecting fill media, heat exchangers, and other components from scaling, fouling, or inefficient operation.

IoT Conductivity Check: Automated controllers should continuously monitor and maintain Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) levels. The target is a precise 2,800 µS/cm. This prevents scale formation, which insulates heat transfer surfaces and drastically reduces efficiency.
Motor Analysis: Your drive systems, including fans and pumps, are major energy consumers. You must verify that your motors meet the TIS 866-2561 standard for IE3 or IE4 efficiency classes.

Nozzle Distribution Mapping: We identify and correct “dry spots” on the fill media. These areas allow air to bypass the water, a phenomenon known as thermal bypass. It is a common cause of lost thermal efficiency in modern cooling towers. A comprehensive audit ensures uniform water coverage for optimal heat exchange.
This prevents the release of aerosolized pathogens like Legionella and conserves water. Worn or damaged drift eliminators must be replaced immediately.

Rapid qPCR DNA Testing: The traditional 14-day culture method for Legionella detection is too slow. We use real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) testing. This DNA-based analysis provides same-day results, allowing for immediate remediation and preventing dangerous outbreaks.

Biocide Rotation: We have shifted to using biodegradable, PFAS-free biocidal agents. This practice is crucial for meeting the new 2026 industrial discharge bylaws, which strictly regulate water pollutants. Rotating biocides also prevents microorganisms from developing resistance.
FRP Integrity Scan: We replace corroded steel components with Pultruded Fiber-Reinforced Polymer (FRP). Regular scans confirm the integrity of the tower’s framework.
